applied_settings: ***TUNED - SPLIT-REGION CURVE (Afterburner Profile 5) + MEMORY +2500, POWER LIMIT 111% = 200 W. NOT STOCK.*** REPLICATE of splitcurve-suite-20260907 (s1), collected to give the tuned configuration an interval - s1 was n=1 and the 27.4% mean efficiency gain it reports carries no spread at all, while the stock side has five replicates. CONFIGURATION VERIFIED TWO WAYS BEFORE LAUNCH, not assumed: (a) the Afterburner profile store on disk was DECODED - Profile 5 holds MemClkBoost +2500, PowerLimit 111, and a V/F curve that follows the stock slope low down (1447 MHz at 700 mV, 2180 at 850 mV) then pins flat at 3030 MHz from about 925 mV upward, which is the split-region shape; (b) probed under load, peak memory 16301 MHz and peak core 3022 MHz against this card's signatures of stock ~2593, full tune ~2947, split ~2977. Driver 616.64. Launched at 39 C after a 15-MINUTE MINIMUM COOLDOWN following r8. The wait is gated on TIME, not on temperature: temperature.gpu is the die sensor and returns to idle in 2-3 minutes on this card while the heatsink, VRM and memory are still shedding heat, and temperature.memory reads N/A here, so no available sensor reports the slow thermal mass. A temperature-gated wait would have fired after ~3 minutes and looked principled while controlling almost nothing. 38 C is s1's launch temperature, so s2 starts from the same thermal state as the run it is compared against. OPERATOR WAS AWAY FROM THE MACHINE for this run; the curve was applied programmatically with 'MSIAfterburner.exe -profile5 -q' rather than by hand, which is a first for this project and is recorded here because it changes who verified what. WARNING: if the display driver resets mid-run it SILENTLY CLEARS the Afterburner offsets (recorded 2026-08-30), so a sweep collected after such an event would measure STOCK silicon under this settings string - the post-run probe and the per-sweep achieved clocks are the check.
